subject: Control plane / data plane handshake — reference diagrams and questions
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: James Liu <james.liu@atlasdata.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@datacenterpartners.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Control plane / data plane handshake — reference diagrams and questions

Hi James / Sarah,

Attaching a first-pass set of reference diagrams for the private deployment we discussed (redwood_vpc_refdiagrams_v1.pdf) and a simple controlplane↔dataplane mapping spreadsheet (controlplane_dataplane_mapping_v2.xlsx). These are intentionally high-level; we want to validate assumptions before we lock CIDR ranges and BGP session plans.

Top-level assumptions:
- Customer will host data-plane nodes (in their VPC/colo). Redwood control plane will be reachable over a private transit (VPN or dedicated interconnect).
- Control plane communication uses mTLS (mutual certs) to an IP/port range we'll publish; no public-key-based access.
- Data-plane outbound to model downloads and container registry will be via customer-provided egress (we can also provide an approved mirror if egress is restricted).

Questions for your ops team (short, actionable):
1) Preferred connectivity: site-to-site VPN (IKEv2) or BGP over private interconnect? If interconnect, what ASN and /29s can you reserve for the control plane?
2) Do you have an egress proxy requirement (HTTP proxy auth or transparent)? If so, can it perform TLS interception for downloads (we prefer an approved S3/OCI mirror to avoid interception).
3) KMS/HSM: will keys for token encryption live in your KMS, or do we use a customer-managed HSM with Redwood side of the key zeroed?
4) Audit logs: can you accept an encrypted syslog stream to port 6514 (TLS)? Or do you need a pull-based collection?

Requested next steps:
- Please review the two attachments and comment on the CIDR/bgp columns (sheet tab: \"mapping-v2\").
- If possible, share a contact from your network team we can do a short 30m call with this week.

Thanks — Mateo

--
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_vpc_refdiagrams_v1.pdf (PDF, 6 pages); controlplane_dataplane_mapping_v2.xlsx (Excel, 2 tabs)

From: James Liu <james.liu@atlasdata.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@datacenterpartners.io>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Control plane / data plane handshake — reference diagrams and questions

Mateo — thanks for the docs. Quick answers from our side and a few follow-ups.

1) Connectivity: we prefer BGP over a private interconnect for predictability. We can reserve a /29 for your control-plane peer. I'll confirm exact ASN by EOD.
2) Egress proxy: yes, we run an auth-enabled HTTP proxy for all outbound. We do not allow TLS interception. If Redwood can provide a signed mirror for model artifacts (S3 or OCI), that will be necessary.
3) KMS: keys must remain in our KMS (HashiCorp Vault backed by our HSM). We require that any token or persistent secret material is encrypted by our KMS before it leaves our network.
4) Audit logs: we can accept encrypted syslog (TLS) to port 6514; we prefer push over pull.

Open items:
- Port/endpoint whitelist: can you publish the exact IPs and ports the control plane will talk to? We need them for firewall rules.
- Local metrics: can the data plane export Prometheus metrics to our scrape endpoint, or do you require pull through a metrics proxy?

I'll loop in our network engineer (cc'd) on the BGP details once I have ASN. Also happy to join a 30m call tomorrow afternoon PST — 1:00pm or 3:00pm work for me.

Thanks,
James

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Control plane / data plane handshake — reference diagrams and questions

James — thanks, good context. Quick clarifications from our infra side (copying Jonas for technical detail):

- IP/ports: we will provide a published set of IPs (single /29) and these ports: 443 (control plane mTLS), 8443 (agent bootstrap), 6514 (syslog/TLS). We will provide a short-lived ASN peering plan during cutover and rotate to long-term ASN afterward.
- Mirror for artifacts: Redwood can host an S3-backed mirror endpoint for model artifacts and container images. We will sign objects and provide a stable host (mirror.atlas.redwood-inference.com). Your proxy can allow that FQDN.
- KMS integration: we support encrypting runtime tokens with customer KMS. In practice: the data-plane agent will request a wrapping key from your Vault endpoint; Redwood control plane will never hold the unwrapped key. We will exchange an OIDC-backed service identity and perform mutual attestation.
- Metrics: our recommended pattern is push metrics via Prometheus pushgateway inside your VPC into your scrape endpoint. If you need direct scraping, we can enable a scrape endpoint bound to the data-plane interface but behind your firewall.

Action items we propose:
1) Redwood to publish a short \"control-plane whitelist\" (IPs + ports) by EOD Wed (24 Nov).
2) Atlas to confirm proxy ACL for mirror.FQDN and confirm ASN for peering.
3) Schedule 30m call — proposed times (PST): Tue 24 13:00 or 15:00. Mateo and Jonas will join.

Jonas — can you add a brief runbook note in the mapping sheet about BGP communities + OSPF fallback? I started the runbook tab with a few bullet points.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Network PM, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

- Confirmed: we will allow mirror.atlas.redwood-inference.com through our proxy (we'll add an ACL for the FQDN).
- ASN: 64523 will be the peer ASN; Atlas will provide the /29 for your side (please use the one you publish in the whitelist).
- Syslog: we will accept TLS syslog to a collector at syslog.ops@atlasdata.com (port 6514) — I attached our collector cert thumbprint in the calendar invite.

Let's do the call at Tue 24 13:00 PST (I meant Tue 24 Nov — apologies for timezone slip; if that doesn't work for Redwood folks please propose Wed morning PST). I've also uploaded a short network inventory sheet to your Drive folder (see link).

I will prepare a brief BGP playbook (peers, auth, communities) and drop it into JIRA SUP-9812 before the meeting.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

James
